messages.subject: [Ipmpack-users] IPMpack v1.5
messages.body_plain:
Dear IPMpack-users,

v1.5 is now online. This version has some new features and fixes based 
on the IPM summer course in Rostock a few weeks ago. In order to run 
IPMpack v1.5 correctly, PLEASE MAKE SURE YOU HAVE INSTALLED THE 'Matrix' 
PACKAGE VERSION 1.0-9. Otherwise you might run into errors concerning 
the superclass 'mMatrix'.

best wishes,
Eelke

IPMpack: http://ipmpack.r-forge.r-project.org/
binaries: http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/IPMpack/index.html

IPMpack v1.5 has new sensitivity functions (for life expectancy, R0, 
etc) and createIntegerPmatrix lets you build population transition 
models with integer stages only, based on various vital rate models. 
We've made further improvements to amongst others the functions 
makeFecObj, makeDiscreteTrans and elas. The survival and growth matrix 
is now called /Pmatrix/ (previously /Tmatrix/) as suggested by a 
reviewer. The makeFecObj and similar functions now have a /Formula/ slot 
in which the regression formula (e.g. nPups~size) can be entered.)

messages.subject: [Ipmpack-users] Help with IPMpack
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody!

I hope you're very well. I write you because I have some questions about
IPMpack.

I will introduce you my project:

I'm studying the demography of a tropical palm in  Mexico,  I have data of
this specie for: Growth (in centimeters), survival and  fecundity, i've
been running this data from IPMpack and everything is OK.

Now I want introduce a new measure of growth because this specie has a very
slow-growth when is an infant and it hasn't a measurable lenght. I have
data for: number of leaves, and i thing it can explain me this growth when
the palm hasn't lenght, i.e. I want to construct a compound Pmatrix with
functions for growth and survival for number of seeds (discrete stage) and
with funtions for growth and survival for lenght (continuous stage), the
fecundity just will be in the continuous stage.

I've been reviewing the IPMpack manual, but I misunderstood so well how to
do it in the same environment, i.e. just with 1 env. (without covariables).

Someone have and idea to do this?


Thanks, :)

*Iv?n Alejandro Ortiz Rodr?guez*

Lab. de Ecolog?a de Poblaciones y Comunidades Tropicales
Centro de Investigaciones en Ecosistemas, UNAM-Campus Morelia

messages.subject: [Ipmpack-users] Help with IPMpack
messages.body_plain:
Dear Iv?n,

Depending on how variable the number of leaves of juveniles, you either 
would want to include the number of leaves of juveniles as a continuous 
state variable (but IPMpack does not include the possibility yet to have 
more than 1 continuous state variable), or have the number of juvenile 
leaves as 1 or more discrete stages next to the continuous state 
variable palm height. Please have a look at functions like 
makeDiscreteTrans for examples.

best wishes,
Eelke

messages.body_plain:
Hello all, we are trying to implement the procedure in section 8 of the vignette with no luck.  We try to run the code as written, we get this output:


tmp <- optim(c(1, 1, 1), wrapSaturate, dataf = dff, method = "Nelder-Mead")

Error in +u <- exp(pmin(pars[1] + pars[2] * size, 50)) :
  object 'u' not found

> tmp
Error: object 'tmp' not found
>


I am sure we are forgetting to do something painfully obvious.  Could a user of the list point us in the right direction?  Thanks for any insights.

Best,

Emilio
